[quote=the_crystalline_empire;61627618][b]July 23, 2028: The Second Convention of Secession[/b]

I see the duc of Mittlemarkke has made himself unavailable once again, intoned Erjk Drs.

Unfortunately yes, I heard you ran a public poll on secession in Thýven, mentioned the duc of Knygta and Deyn.

Yes, two military officers have been watching me, the poll is online however, and we have restricted it to only citizens of Thýven, replied the duc of Thýven.

How is it faring? Asked the duc of Westmarkke.

Better than expected, reorganizing our territory to include the lands Rosenmarkke annexed back in January helps a lot, laughed Erjk Drs.

How about the Estate Legislature? Asked the duc of Westmarkke.

Some of our members have been arrested, and there are unionists who are operating sub-groups in the capital, replied the duc.

Secession is a risky business, right now Knygta and Deyn plans on seceding on August 1st, but we need to first gain assurances from the armed forces that are losing their loyalty that their operations later this week will work, replied the duc of Knygta and Deyn.

Mittlemarkke has no doubt informed the government, intoned Westmarkke.

Yes, which is why it is my hope the Strømmists are engaged in other matters, replied Knygta and Deyn.

Belgarde, smiled Westmarkke.

Exactly,

 Eyh, remind me, the islands sovietised their forces during the war no? Asked Thýven.

Yes, they did, replied Knygta and Deyn.

Did the government ever order them to reorganise? Thýven asked.

No, its actually why we have loyalists to Unionism in our region, or at least strong opposition to the Rosenmarkket government, the islands have always been their own thing, chuckled Knygta and Deyn.

As has Thýven, but, you are the largest economic sector, replied Thýven, Your leaving will cripple the regime politically at least, 

The markets have been closed since the massacre, the economy according to independent analysts is in recession right now, investors have fled since the war, replied Knygta and Deyn.

What a mess, sighed the duc of Thýven.

Well its about to get better, smiled Knygta and Deyn.

We hope, replied Westmarkke.

[b]July 24, 2025: Rumors of secession[/b]

It had started as an internet blog a week before, and quickly flooded the Rosenmarkket and Montfleurois internet to the point where local news stations were beginning to report on it, secession.

While the government of Rosenmarkke openly denied any such movement, and blamed it on Wuloosyan bad actors the evidence that could be sleuthed out in the regions was enough to make a conclusion that even if secession wasnt occurring something was.

As protests continued across the country, driven by the momentum of the massacre earlier in the month, there had begun to be signs of military non-compliance. For instance in one protest in the Thývenic city of Gossen, the guards that had been ordered into the city by the government were reported to be avoiding the protests that were forming, or in some cases actively joining them,

Then there were the indicators, independent polling taken between July 20-24 showed that out a poll of around 1,300 Rosenmarkket from across the country, support for the government was at 44% a radical and steep drop from the 75-80% that had occurred during the war against Wuloosya.

The government was loosing legitimacy, and to most, it had become clear that this was the case, the declaration had done things that no-one couldve predicted. 

The question now for most was When?, because in more autonomous regions it seemed that they were ready to leap from the nation into secession, however, the more cautious public voices warned of economic collapse and foreign attack.

So what was true? When was it to occur? And most importantly, how?


[b]July 25, 2028: The Admiral[/b]

The docks of Vysjllá held an eerie calm as the early morning rays fell upon the cranes and warehouses that lined the waters front. Guards had been positioned at these docks by the government, primarily due to concerns of an attempted defection by naval officers and sailors that had been rumored to be planned. 

The admiral of the third fleet, which had been docked in Vysjllá before the war, and now held the remains of the third fleet including the countries only remaining frigate, was a stern man and a native to the islands, his family had lived on the islands for centuries according to the family geneaology.

Ivar Iverkythe walked along the docks where the nations only frigate sat quietly, a fake order for the sailors to ready the ship for a trip to the port of Tharkønn had allowed for the ship to be cleanly crewed. Arriving at the gangway of the ship, he showed his identification papers to the guards stationed at the bottom, two young men who clearly had wished to other things than stand guard over a ship.

Gentlemen, thank you for your service, you may go now, smiled the admiral.

Sir, I am afraid we have orders not to leave this post until the commanding officer sends an order, replied one of the guards.

I am the commanding officer? Stated the Admiral, confused.

We need orders from the capital sir, there have been rumors of defections and some of the leadership has been arrested, said the second guard.

Ivar frowned, this had not been the plan, Gentlemen, who gave you the order?

We cannot give you that information, replied the first guard.

Ivar heard the sound of cars pulling up to the dock, turning to look at the cars he noted that these were government cars, perhaps this was the mysterious higher-up.

His stomach sank as he saw who stepped out of the car, dressed in a simple suit and tie, it was Iosef Begren, the new head of the SCSID, appointed two weeks prior, and allegedly according to underground networks the key figure in the massacre of July 16.

Admiral, how odd it is that we should meet, began Begren with a cruel smile.

I was hoping to see you, I have an order to get this ship to Tharkønn, replied Ivar calmly.

Begren laughed, What order? No order was given by the High Admiral of the Navy? 

Ivar realised suddenly that he had been outmaneuvered.

I can tell by your beautiful face, that you are aware of this? Smiled Begren.

I was not, 

Yes it was released last night, all forces will be centralised once more, with the defection rumors and all of that, we cannot have a disorganized armed forces, replied Begren.

I see, 

Which brings me to our little problem, there is no order to Tharkønn, so why is your ship crewed? This is an answer we shall never know, because I already know it replied Begren, reaching into his coat-pocket and pulling out a pistol.

N-no! Cried the admiral as the gun went off and he crumpled to the ground, dead.

Arrest the crew, stated Begren, Execute them, and shove their bodies off the dock, he said to the SCSID officers who had just stepped out of the cars.

[b]Emergency planning[/b]

The admiral failed, began the duc of Knygta and Deyn moving to sit himself in the booth of a highway restaurant, the duc of Thýven already reading the menu.

I heard, this new SCSID head, Bergen, I am concerned about him, he seems to be a pretty hardline loyalist, replied Thýven.

Hes already got officers at my offices, and the order to de-sovietise the army, that was a slick move, replied Knygta and Deyn.

The duc of Thýven frowned, What does this mean for us? he asked.

It means, that were going to have to either speed up or slow down, replied the duc of Knygta and Deyn, What matters is how rash Haakon acts, or how willing the people are, 

Thýven sighed, So what are our plans?

We continue, just stretch the timeline, move more carefully, placate the state, replied Knygta and Deyn.

Any word on Montfleur? asked Thýven.

Radio silence, replied Knygta and Deyn.

What about the association? asked Thýven.

Most of them have been quietly moved into Montfleur, r

Hm, nodded Thýven.

The assembly will vote today on the measures proposed by the king, replied Knygta and Deyn.

Well, lets hope this goes well, sighed Thýven rising from the table.

[b]Montfleur[/b]

Henri and Eleonore walked into the brightly lit interior of the Bojerries restaurant, a fastfood chain native to Wuloosya, but a regional favorite in the cosmopolitan capital of Montfleur. Eleonore had tried to persuade Henri from meeting at Bojerries, but the king could not be dissuaded on this matter.

Theyve begun centralising, intoned Henri as they stood in line, getting curious looks from the patrons of the restaurant.

The regime? asked Eleonore.

Yes, replied Henri, Weve been getting radio silence from some of the people we have been in contact with, I am concerned,

The line moved forward slowly.

Its looking increasingly like they are waiting for us to move, I do not doubt they are planning retaliation for our supporting the secession, replied Eleonore.

Which is why we need the vote today, 

Eleonore nodded as the line moved forward again, peering at the menu with a frown.

Have you tried the Cajun Filet Biscuit? asked Henri, looking at the menu.

No, I dont like the biscuit, replied Eleonore, I like the bone in-fried chicken combo, 

I dont know I am considering the Grilled Chicken Club, they say Grilled chicken is healthier, replied Henri.

I was just looking at that, state Eleonore with a nod, Anyways,

Yes, anyways, the fact of the matter is that we are looking at an extremely volatile situation, my red line speech, which was brilliant by the way, shouldve shocked these people a little, continued Henri

They finally arrived at the head of the line, where a stunned cashier stopped mid-sentence at the sight of the king and the head of the government standing there. 

Uh, yeah, wed like the Grilled Chicken Club? Lets make that a combo? said Henri.

Your majesty, stated the girl who was clearly some college student who needed a day job. 

Ill be paying for the both of it, continued Henri ignoring the girls shock.

She quickly put in the order, gave the cost, and Henri and Eleonore shuffled away to a booth to wait for their order to arrive.

Well probably have to leave quickly, the vote happens inthirty minutes, replied Eleonore looking at her watch.

Yes indeed, anyways, if we deploy the Gendarme, and Rosenmarkke indeed does attack, began Henri.

Itll justify a fuller intervention, of course I shant discuss the details here, laughed Eleonore, looking around at the crowded restaurant.

Henri nodded as the server came over and set down the trays of food before them, and they began to eat following a prayer.
